attacks.claim: Offline expiry is judged on device time. The only backstop is a check against download-time server time, which catches only a clock set before download. A clock set back to a time after download, or one that drifts behind real time, still shows a forecast past valid_until in color. That breaks the agreed rule that stale safety information is never shown as current.
attacks.evidence: "The expiry rule above applies on-device using device time... if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired." QA covers only "Device clock moved earlier than offline download time."

attacks.claim: The artifact does not bound CDN cache TTL against valid_until. Expiry is stated server-side only for the API, so a CDN-cached response could serve an expired rating in color to clients that do not re-check valid_until. The CDN-cached path is excluded from rate-limit counting, so it is not otherwise checked.
attacks.evidence: "If WADE is unreachable, our API keeps serving forecasts still inside `valid_until`" and "serves zone geometry + ratings from our CDN"; ABSENT: CDN TTL relative to valid_until.

attacks.claim: The cutover sequence is inconsistent. The flag goes to 100% at 08:00 while the blog post and in-app card wait until 10:00 for an undefined 'check that all 19 centers render.' Layer data is live to all users for two hours with no defined gate, and the public blog post cannot be recalled once published.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 23 08:00: flag on for 100%. Blog post and in-app card go live at 10:00 after a check that all 19 centers render."

attacks.claim: The rollback claim is overstated. Remote config applies only on next foreground, and the offline purge runs only on launch, so an offline phone that is not opened keeps its cached flag and colored ratings. The artifact's 'no stale ratings remain on phones' is therefore not true until the app next runs.
attacks.evidence: "Set `avalanche_layer=false` (remote config, takes effect on next app foreground)... so no stale ratings remain on phones." and QA: "offline forecast data purged on next launch."

attacks.claim: Removing a center through config leaves its offline copies colored until valid_until. The artifact does not show that this satisfies the agreement if a center asks the app to stop displaying its forecast, and the agreement's withdrawal terms are not cited.
attacks.evidence: "its zones disappear within 10 min and any offline copies expire at their `valid_until`"

attacks.claim: Screen-reader behavior was tested only for a current forecast. The safety-relevant 'Forecast expired' and 'No current forecast' states have no recorded VoiceOver or TalkBack announcement test.
attacks.evidence: "VoiceOver / TalkBack: zone announced as \"[zone], danger 3 Considerable, issued [time]\"; card fully readable; 200% text | Pass" (no expired or no-forecast case)

attacks.claim: Issue and valid-until times are displayed without a specified time zone, even though the 19 centers span US and Canadian zones. A user in another zone could misread when a safety forecast expires.
attacks.evidence: "the issue time, the valid-until time" and "Forecast expired [time]" and "issued [time]" (no time-zone format given)

attacks.claim: Public store notes for 6.12 omit the layer, while App Review notes describe it and the review build had it enabled. Users who update on Nov 19 may find the layer appear without store-note disclosure. This is a messaging inconsistency, not a safety defect, since the flag is off until Nov 23.
attacks.evidence: "public store notes do not mention the layer yet. App Review notes for 6.12 describe the layer and the remote flag, and the review build had it enabled."

attacks.claim: bbox quantization or tiling is not specified. Arbitrary bbox values fragment the CDN cache, which undermines the 92% hit-rate and $140/month origin projection. The cost math also has no stated assumption for the 100% rollout peak.
attacks.evidence: "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" and "Projected 1.8M zone requests/day at 92% CDN hit rate; origin cost ~$140/month"; ABSENT: bbox rounding or tiling scheme.

attacks.claim: The 120 req/min per-IP origin limit may throttle legitimate users behind carrier NAT or shared IPs. The artifact does not say how a 429 is rendered, so a throttled zone could fail in an unclear way.
attacks.evidence: "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP (CDN-cached responses are not counted)"

attacks.claim: Center-removal propagation is asserted as '10 min' without naming the deploy or config path that makes this true, and the artifact gives no verification step for a center's stop request.
attacks.evidence: "A single center can be removed by editing `config/avy_centers.json`... its zones disappear within 10 min"

attacks.claim: 'No location' is overstated. The bbox query and the zone id on card open reveal the user's viewport and area, which is location-adjacent in backcountry use.
attacks.evidence: "Network capture: no location in avalanche requests or analytics | Pass" alongside "requests forecasts by zone id for the visible map tiles"

attacks.claim: Attribution appears only in the tap-opened card. The agreement requires attribution, and the artifact does not show whether the map layer or legend carries it.
attacks.evidence: "we must attribute and link to the issuing center" (attribution shown in "a summary card")
